hints: Notice the word not in bold, so you must find the three true statements of Newton's first, second and third laws and select the remaining one.

Recall how each law is worded: constant velocity with no resultant force, rate of change of momentum $\Delta p/\Delta t$ proportional to force, and equal and opposite forces on two interacting bodies X and Y.
Compare the total momentum of a system statement with the three laws to decide whether it is a law itself or a consequence that follows when there is no external force.
walkthrough: List what Newton's three laws state: first law links zero resultant force to constant velocity, second law links resultant force to rate of change of momentum, third law links the force of X on Y to the force of Y on X.
Check the equal and opposite force statement for bodies X and Y. It is the action-reaction pair acting on different bodies, so it matches Newton's third law.
Check the no resultant force and constant velocity statement. With $F = 0$ there is no acceleration, so velocity is unchanged, which matches Newton's first law.

Check the rate of change of momentum statement. It states change is proportional to resultant force and in the same direction, which matches Newton's second law in the form $F \propto \Delta p/\Delta t$.

The remaining statement about total momentum of a system staying constant with no external force is true physics but it is the conservation of momentum, a consequence of the laws, not one of Newton's three laws. This is option D.

options.A: This is Newton's third law, as it describes the equal and opposite action-reaction pair when body X acts on body Y.
options.B: This is Newton's first law, as zero resultant force means no acceleration so velocity stays constant.
options.C: This is Newton's second law, as $F$ equals rate of change of momentum in the direction of the resultant force.
options.D: This is the principle of conservation of momentum, which can be derived from Newton's laws but is not itself stated as one of the three laws.
